title: A B Corp operator reads the SEC's move on shareholder proposals through the book — 'who gets a say in how a company is run'
summary: The SEC has proposed rescinding Rule 14a-8, which since 1942 has let any shareholder put a proposal to a vote at a company's annual meeting. Hirons runs HigherRing, a certified B Corp and public benefit corporation, and is filing a comment against it before the 20 November deadline.
blockquote: I’ve been thinking about this alongside Eric Ries’s book Incorruptible, which looks at why good companies go bad and how the great ones stay great. A big part of that is who gets a say in how a company is run. Shareholder proposals give long-term owners a way to ask a board to look hard at a risk before it turns into a problem.
